_descriptor_type: A type of descriptor. One of 'simulation', 'trace', and 'perf'.
_architecture: A name of the available architectures (PARAMS.<architecture>) found in scarab repository, which defines the machine parameters of the default configuration.
_experiment: The name of the experiment. scarab-infra will create a new folder named containing all files needed to execute the simulation in the <ROOT_DIR>/simulations/<experiment> directory. The folder will also contain all generated simulation statistics/outputs.
_workload_manager: manual: run each exp scenario with all the simpoints at a time, slurm: Slurm schedules simulations based on its policy
_root_dir: Root directory mounted into the docker container home, for instance, the user's home directory
_application_dir: The path to the benchmark application directory used for tracing or simulation.
_scarab_path: The path to the scarab repository that contains the scarab binary used to run the experiment. Must be built from the td-load-rrip-min-extrapolate branch (adds td_combined_dynamic_depth + per-class extreme depths td_combined_dyn_instr_extreme / td_combined_dyn_data_extreme).
_traces_dir: The local directory containing all simpointed traces
_top_simpoint: Run only top 3 simpoints stored in 'workloads_top_simp.json'.
_simulations: Combined L2 dynamic-depth with GRADUATED buckets. The global depth is chosen from the top-down slot-level Frontend-vs-Memory-Bound balance (fe_frac), quantized into td_combined_dyn_buckets buckets over [0,1]; each class's depth is interpolated basic (its far end) -> suite max (middle) -> extreme (its near end), so every bucket toward an end pushes that class more extreme and the other toward basic. Per-line RRPVs still use the cycle-level per-miss fraction (localization). Depths: suite max instr -48 / data -32; extremes swept. Window 100k, thresholds pinned (instr 0.7 / data 0.5). Compare IPC / ICACHE_MISS / DCACHE_MISS_LD vs. baseline.
_configurations: baseline = untouched L2. static_both = both at suite max always (reference). gradN_* = graduated dynamic depth with N buckets and the given per-class extreme (interpolated basic..suite max..extreme). 8 buckets is the default granularity; grad4/grad16 vary it. All gradN_* configs span the buckets over the [fe_lo,fe_hi]=[0.3,0.95]: fe_lo=0.3 (==0.7 membound) floors the deepest data-favoring bucket and fe_hi=0.95 caps at the most FE-bound workloads. Tune fe_lo/fe_hi to the min/max fe_frac reported by plot_boundness_breakdown.py. Data extreme is pinned at -64 (the deepest data-favoring bucket, bucket 0), so the sweep now varies the instruction extreme and bucket count with data's peak depth held at -64.

static_both._params: HEADLINE: instructions -48 AND data -32 together (both at their effective depth; non-zero-sum test).

grad8_mod._params: Graduated dynamic depth: 8 buckets, moderate extreme. Suite max -48/-32, window 100k; bucket window [0.3,0.95] (fe_lo=0.3 == 0.7 membound floors the most-data-favoring bucket; fe_hi=0.95 = the ~95%-FE workloads).65-membound population).

grad8_deep._params: Graduated dynamic depth: 8 buckets, deep extreme. Suite max -48/-32, window 100k; bucket window [0.3,0.95] (fe_lo=0.3 == 0.7 membound floors the most-data-favoring bucket; fe_hi=0.95 = the ~95%-FE workloads).65-membound population).

grad8_deeper._params: Graduated dynamic depth: 8 buckets, deeper extreme. Suite max -48/-32, window 100k; bucket window [0.3,0.95] (fe_lo=0.3 == 0.7 membound floors the most-data-favoring bucket; fe_hi=0.95 = the ~95%-FE workloads).65-membound population).

grad16_deep._params: Graduated dynamic depth: 16 buckets (finer), deep extreme. Suite max -48/-32, window 100k; bucket window [0.3,0.95] (fe_lo=0.3 == 0.7 membound floors the most-data-favoring bucket; fe_hi=0.95 = the ~95%-FE workloads).65-membound population).

grad4_deep._params: Graduated dynamic depth: 4 buckets (coarser), deep extreme. Suite max -48/-32, window 100k; bucket window [0.3,0.95] (fe_lo=0.3 == 0.7 membound floors the most-data-favoring bucket; fe_hi=0.95 = the ~95%-FE workloads).65-membound population).

_collect_stats: Stats collection settings for ./sci --collect-stats. configs: optional list of configuration names to collect (null or omitted = all configurations).
_visualize: Visualization settings for ./sci --visualize. Configure baseline and counters.
_mem: Memory scheduling and collection settings for Slurm jobs.
